title: Prehospital Use of Ultrasound in Undifferentiated Shortness of Breath
brief_summary: This is a pilot observational feasibility study of the ability of paramedics to assess thoracic ultrasound findings in the prehospital environment. The primary goal of the study is to determine whether paramedics are able to accurately assess for sonographic B-lines in patients with undifferentiated shortness of breath at least 80% of the time in the prehospital environment using a portable ultrasound (U/S) device.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

\- Dyspnea and any of the following:

* Respiratory rate \> 20
* Room air oxygen saturation \< 92%
* Accessory muscle use, tripod position, nasal flaring
* Exam with evidence of rales/rhonchi or wheezing
* In acute respiratory distress on paramedic evaluation
* Any patient in acute respiratory distress with

Exclusion Criteria:

* Trauma
* Burns
* Pregnancy
* Kussmaul respirations from metabolic acidosis
* Cheyne-stokes from increased ICP (intracranial pressure), heart failure or CVA
* Drowning
